notes: PLAN.md tier 9 section 9.3, class EX: no Python counterpart, and a faithful C++ reimplementation of Stripenn 1.1.65.22's own detection method (project owner directive, see cpp/tools/stripes_impl.hpp). This tiny committed fixture is a mechanics sanity check (argument parsing, cool loading, exit status, no crash), not a statistical validation; the recall and precision gate of PLAN.md 9.3 is measured on real GM12878 data by cpp/scripts/stripe_calibration.py, which is far too large to commit (cpp/AGENTS_CONTRACT.md rule 10). --pValue 1.0 --fdr 1.0 keeps every candidate here since this fixture's chromosomes are too sparse to give a meaningful background sample. memory.budget_mb 288: the null distribution is estimated from all chromosomes of the matrix as Stripenn does, so every chromosome is held as a band of 2*400 + 2*background + 24 bins around the diagonal (844 bins at 5 kb, 38 MB for the largest chromosome here); the default alpha/beta budget of 64.9 MB for this 0.17 MB input does not cover that fixed per-chromosome cost.

As the cool case above, but through the h5 whole-matrix loader (no per-chromosome band reader for h5, cpp/tools/hicDetectStripes.cpp mirrors hicDetectLoops' approach: hicx::read_hicexplorer_h5 then hicx::select_bins).
An unknown --chromosomes name exits 1 before anything is written, the same behaviour hicDetectLoops.cpp has for the same condition.
